newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan IC stocks rise on outlook, depreciation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan IC stocks rise on outlook, depreciation.

text.p: Share prices in Taiwan's integrated circuit sector jumped at mid-session Thursday on expectations of sound third-quarter profits and a likely export lift from an easier Taiwan dollar, brokers said.
With 70 minutes left, at 0250 GMT, Taiwan Semiconductor was up T$2.50 or 2.38 percent to T$107.50 and United Microelectronics rose T$2.50 or 3.70 percent to T$70.

Many investors had dumped IC shares after their stellar rise in Taiwan's first-quarter bull run and an announcement of less than spectacular first-quarter results. But brokers now say they are optimistic about the microchip industry's outlook.
"The third quarter is the traditional hot sales season for IC companies. Many IC companies still have potential to rise," said Chen Han-chung, an analyst of Yungli Securities.
Brokers said a recent gradual depreciation of the Taiwan dollar also helped boost confidence for the electronics industry, whose lifeblood is exports.
